posts.cooked:
Back to the usual stuff. Setback, Argent Adept and Captain Cosmic fell to advanced Voss in the Realm of Discord.
 
Random is being weird. :| Advanced Kismet absolutely annihilated the Scholar, GI Bunker, Haka and Setback in the Realm of Discord.
 
Okay, I guess it's Realm of Discord day! Chrono-Ranger, DW Fixer and Horus Ra against Iron Legs in the Realm. It was a short, fast game, and they actually won because Chrono is awesome against Iron Legacy. :D
 
What's this? No Realm of Discord? GI Bunker, TLT and Legacy versus the Dreamer at Megalopolis. They didn't last very long. :/
 
Okay, Setback, Legacy and Tachyon versus advanced Gloomweaver in Megalopolis. Still in a rut! Almost the entire battle was fought on the roof, Setback knocked himself out because Legacy pushed him too hard, but Tachyon was able to blitz down the relics as fast as they came out. Good stuff!
 
Time to test some stuff out. Xtreme Prime Wardens Argent Adept, EWAZ and [REDACTED] against Akash'Bhuta in the Celestia Tribunal. Various repesentatives for Earth included Dr. Medico, America's Youngest Legacy, and America's Greatest Legacy, because I figured out how to game that particular card. :V Hour and a half game, but lots of good team support saw the heroes to victory!
 
The Sentinels, Bunker, and Hunted Naturalist faced Chokepoint at the Temple of Zhu Long. (If I'd played Setback, it would've been Preview Pack 2 in physical! :V) It was a surprisingly long game, but a combination of Preadtor's Eye and Bunker's ridiculous damage bonuses took her down on her flip side.
 
Next, Setting Sun Ra, Haka and the Argent Adept faced the Ennead in the Ruins of Atlantis. Ra blazed like a fire, and the villains were taken down. Ra survived with 3 HP.
 
Last, Mr. Fixer, Tempest and Redeemer Fanatic versus Apostate in the Celestial Tribunal. America's Greatest Legacy was called to represent Earth. Teamwork (and disgusting holy nukes) saved the day.

Old college friend got Sentinels digitally (base game, another friend gifted him mini-pack 1), so we got on Skype and played a couple games to teach him how to play.

 

Baron Blade is trying to bring down the moon in Insula Primalis! Luckily, Grandpa Legacy, Tachyon, and Absolute Zero were there to teach the volcano how to chill. (First game I've played with Zero that he started with Isothermic Transducer, Focused Apertures, Cold Snap, and drew into Null-Point Calibration Unit and Thermal Shockwave within the first few turns. That game was insane.)

Then, Ambuscade wanted a shootout in Silver Gulch. Unity, Bunker: Engine of War, and The Wraith were happy to oblige him.

Finally, Fanatic, Wraith, and Ra failed to stop Grand Warlord Voss from Invading from the Ruins of Atlantis after he discovered the Pillars of Hercules and got out the majority of his deck. However, with an End of Days, Fanatic went down with a bang...taking out all of Voss's ground troops, both starships, his Quark translocators, and the Pillars in one final Blast...

Ra was really impressed.

Next, the Temple of Zhu Long was having a Plague Rat problem, so they called in Hunted Naturalist, DW Expatriette, Freedom Five Bunker, DW Fixer and Beardy Ra to exterminate. Expatriette fell, but was revived soon after, and Fixer of course wrecked house. The finishing blow was a massive Omni-Cannon strike.
 
Next, Xtreme Tempest, the Scholar and Fanatic went chasing Wager Master through the Realm of Discord. (What's that? A game without the Naturalist? My briefcase full of Naturalists should put a stop to that!) The heroes won in three rounds thanks to Losing to the Odds.
 
Next, that same team joined up with Engine of War Bunker to take on [REDACTED] in the Court of Blood. Many vampires were slain, Bunker had a field day, and once more got the final blow with the Omnicannon.
 
Lastly, Hunted Naturalist came back to help the Scholar, Setback and [REDACTED] chase Omnitron through time to Silver Gulch! It was a long game, but again, the Naturalist's environment clamp helped save the day. He even got to eat the last drone.

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
First time playing the physical game, and it turned into a lengthy and exciting battle.

Setback, Bunker and the Sentinels took on Gloomweaver and his cult in the Realm of Discord. An early Pouch of Bones and a Vast Following the turn after we destroyed it made it hard for anything to stick (the Profane Zealots didn't help, either) and we spent most of our time just keeping the zombies and cultists at bay thanks to Time Flies -- unfortunately, also thanks to Time Flies, the other two Relics quickly made it out and Gloomweaver flipped. Fortunately by this point, everyone was pretty well set up -- all four Signatures were out, as well as Looking Up, High-Risk Behavior and Silver Lining and Bunker had been reaping obscene amounts of cards thanks to Ammo Drops the whole game.

Writhe's signature got a lot of use. It turns out if Setback is one of the heroes in a 3-H game, Writhe and Mainstay end up as highest HP PDQ (and thanks to their signatures and Dr. Medico, they can stay there a long time). It let Setback keep being High Risky (at one point he had a +4) and kept Gloomweaver punching himself via pins. Things finally broke out for us when -- after the last Vast Following was in the trash -- we killed the Pouch of Bones and we combined for about 50 damage in one round (Yay, Omni-Cannon), Silver-Lining'd Setback to highest HP (he had so many tokens that even with Gloomy's damage reduced to 0, it killed Setback), and finally put Gloomweaver down.

It took us close to two hours, but it was a great time.
